facts.text: Greens Fork takes its name from the Greens Fork River that runs through the town.
The town’s post office has been in operation since 1828, making it one of the oldest continuously running services in the area.
Greens Fork’s growth in the mid‑19th century was spurred by fertile farmlands and the arrival of the railroad, which opened new markets for local farmers.
The Old Millstone Mercantile, a historic general store, still serves as a community hub and local café, welcoming visitors from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays and Saturdays.
In 2002, Greens Fork built a central wastewater treatment plant, a sanitary sewer system, and a lift station to pump sewage to the treatment facility.
The Greens Fork Community Church, an architectural landmark, hosts services on Sundays and offers tours by appointment, reflecting the town’s enduring religious heritage.
